definitions.explanation: Small leftover pieces or fragments from something; materials no longer useful.
A derogatory term for a person considered to be useless or of low character.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}{屑|くず}を{拾|ひろ}って{捨|す}てた。
examples.english: I picked up the scraps of paper and threw them away.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}{屑|くず}はリサイクルできる。
{工場|こうじょう}から{出|で}る{木|き}{屑|くず}を{集|あつ}めて{処分|しょぶん}する。
examples.english: We collect and dispose of the wood shavings from the factory.

examples.japanese: あいつは{人間|にんげん}の{屑|くず}だ。
{約束|やくそく}を{平気|へいき}で{破|やぶ}るなんて、{屑|くず}だと{思|おも}われても{仕方|しかた}ない。
examples.english: If you casually break promises, you can't blame people for thinking you're scum.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}の{屑|くず}と{呼|よ}ばれても、{彼|かれ}は{気|き}にしなかった。
examples.english: Even though he was called the scum of society, he didn't care.

notes:
{屑|くず} means scraps, waste, or refuse. It often appears in compounds referring to specific types of waste material.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {紙|かみ}{屑|くず}: paper scraps
- {鉄|てつ}{屑|くず} / {屑|くず}{鉄|てつ}: scrap iron/metal
- {木|き}{屑|くず}: wood shavings
- {屑|くず}{籠|かご}: wastepaper basket
- パン{屑|くず}: bread crumbs

INSULTING USAGE:
When applied to people, {屑|くず} is extremely derogatory — equivalent to calling someone "scum" or "trash." This usage is common in manga, anime, and online speech, but is very offensive in real life.

WRITING:
Often written in hiragana (くず) or katakana (クズ), especially in the insulting sense. The kanji {屑|くず} appears more in formal or compound usage.
